title: Picard group of a regular-local localization vanishes
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $f\in A$, and let $A_f$ be the localization of $A$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated projective $A_f$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $A_f$ the localization $P_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $(A_f)_{\mathfrak q}$-module of rank one. Then $P\cong A_f$ as $A_f$-modules. (These modules are the invertible $A_f$-modules, so this says $\operatorname{Pic}(A_f)=0$.)

source.place: Tag 0AFZ (more-algebra-lemma-regular-local-Pic-zero), lemma-regular-local-Pic-zero, line 36780, read with Tag 0B8I (more-algebra-lemma-invertible, line 36118: invertible = finite locally free of rank 1) and Tag 00NX (algebra-lemma-finite-projective, line 19027: finite projective = finite locally free)

proof.text: By hypothesis $P$ is a finitely generated projective $A_f$-module whose localization at every prime ideal of $A_f$ is free of rank one. These are exactly the hypotheses imposed on the module in the lemma used in Step 5 (with $S=A_f$), and $P$ is in particular a finitely generated $A_f$-module. (In the language of the source, Tags 0B8I and 00NX, such a $P$ is an invertible $A_f$-module; this identification is not used below.)

source.place: Tag 0AFZ proof opening, read with Tags 0B8I and 00NX

proof.text: Since $P$ is a finitely generated $A_f$-module, apply [lem-trf-localized-finite-module-spread] with $R=A$, the element $f$ and $L=P$ to obtain a finitely generated $A$-module $M$ and an isomorphism of $A_f$-modules $M_f\cong P$.

source.place: Tag 0AFZ proof, line 36789, invoking Algebra Tag 05N5

proof.text: Let $d=\dim A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-module-resolution] the finite $A$-module $M$ has a projective resolution of length at most $d$. Since a regular local ring is a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], [stage3-b4-bounded-finite-free-resolution] applies to $A$, $M$ and $d$ and gives an exact sequence $0\to F_d\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to 0$ with each $F_i$ finite free over $A$, say $F_i\cong A^{r_i}$. Localization at the powers of $f$ is exact (Stacks Tag 00CS) and sends $A^{r_i}$ to $A_f^{r_i}$, so composing with $M_f\cong P$ gives an exact sequence of $A_f$-modules $0\to A_f^{r_d}\to\cdots\to A_f^{r_0}\to P\to 0$.

source.place: Tag 0AFZ proof, line 36790, invoking Proposition Tag 00O7

proof.text: $P$ is a finitely generated projective $A_f$-module with the finite free resolution of Step 3. Therefore [lem-trf-invertible-module-k0-class] with $S=A_f$ and $L=P$ gives $[P]=n[A_f]$ in $K_0(A_f)$ for $n=\sum_i(-1)^ir_i$.
By Step 1, $P$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-trf-k0-class-trivial-invertible] with $S=A_f$, and by Step 4 $[P]=n[A_f]$. That lemma gives $P\cong A_f$ as $A_f$-modules.
